other_uses: A slender native annual bean that twines through prairie grass and sandy open ground across the central United States. Smooth seeds — the feature that separates it from the fuzzy-seeded Strophostyles helvola. Seeds and pods of the genus were gathered and cooked by several Plains and Woodland peoples. A nitrogen-fixing legume: it partners with rhizobia to pull nitrogen out of the air, which is why beans were planted with corn and squash rather than beside them. Native range: the central United States, from the western Great Lakes and the Ohio valley south and west to Texas, New Mexico and Colorado.
prep: Boil the young pods; shell and boil the dry seeds. Small and fiddly, but genuinely food.
soil: Dry sandy or gravelly open ground; prairie, roadside and river sand.
risks: As with all wild beans, cook the seeds thoroughly — do not eat them raw.
